Thanks — below is a 12-week, progressive upper-body strength programme tailored for a 29‑year‑old recreational climber with right subacromial impingement who is 4 months into physio and cleared for pain‑free range only, with no overhead loading. The plan assumes access to a full gym (cables, dumbbells, kettlebells, barbells, machines, pulleys, TRX/strings, pull‑up assist). It prioritises scapular control, rotator cuff and posterior chain strength, avoids overhead loading and end‑range painful positions, and progresses volume and complexity slowly. Each week contains 3 upper‑body sessions (Mon, Wed, Fri) plus 1–2 light lower‑body or full‑body maintenance sessions (optional) focusing on legs and core for climbing transfer. Before starting, confirm the client's physio is comfortable with these exercises and pain‑free execution — if any exercise causes pain at rest or during movement, stop it.

Key principles and precautions
- Only pain‑free range of motion (ROM). Avoid sharp pain, catching, or progressive ache after sessions. Mild transient muscle soreness is acceptable.
- No loaded overhead presses, heavy barbell behind‑neck or wide grip work that raises the shoulder into impingement positions.
- Use rows, horizontal/low to mid‑angle presses, scapular upward/downward control and rotator cuff strengthening (especially external rotation and extension patterns).
- Emphasise posterior shoulder, scapular stabilisers (lower/medial trapezius, serratus anterior), and rotator cuff (infraspinatus, teres minor, subscapularis) with eccentric emphasis as tolerated.
- Start conservative with load and range; progress load, reps, and complexity only when all sets are pain‑free and form is solid.
- Warm‑up before each session: 8–10 minutes light cardio (bike/row), dynamic thoracic mobility, shoulder pendulum and active scapular retraction/protraction drills, 2 light sets of main movement patterns.
- Cool‑down: gentle posterior capsule mobility, doorway pec stretch (pain‑free), and 5–10 minutes icing if recommended by physio and if shoulder is sore post‑session.
- Frequency: 3 sessions focused on upper body; optional 1–2 leg/core sessions to maintain lower‑body strength for climbing.

Progression model
- Weeks 1–4: Foundation — technique, scapular control, rotator cuff activation, low to moderate loads, higher tempo control (3–4 seconds eccentric).
- Weeks 5–8: Build — increase load and complexity, introduce unilateral work and integrated pulling patterns; maintain no overhead loading.
- Weeks 9–12: Strength and power transfer — heavier horizontal/decline pressing, more challenging pulling (weighted or lower assistance), eccentric overload and climbing‑specific scapular endurance. Remain within pain‑free ROM.

Program structure (3 sessions/week). Each session includes:
- Warm‑up (10 min)
- Main strength block (30–40 min)
- Accessory/rotator cuff block (10–15 min)
- Conditioning/core (optional 10 min)
- Cool‑down + mobility

Notation: sets × reps @ RPE or load guidance; tempo: e = eccentric, p = pause, c = concentric (e.g., 3‑0‑1 means 3s down, no pause, 1s up). Rest 60–120s between sets for smaller lifts, 2–3 min for heavier sets.

WEEK 1–4: FOUNDATION
Goal: establish pain‑free patterns, increase scapular endurance, build rotator cuff capacity.

Session A (Mon) — Horizontal Push/Pull emphasis
Warm‑up: 8–10 min bike + shoulder pendulums, 2 light sets of horizontal press and row (e.g., band push and band row).
1. Neutral‑grip dumbbell bench press (flat) — 3 × 8–10, tempo 3‑1‑1, light–moderate load (focus on controlled descent, stop before any shoulder pain).
2. Seated cable row, neutral handle, scapula retraction emphasis — 3 × 10–12, tempo 3‑0‑1.
3. Incline (low incline ~15°) dumbbell press — 2 × 8–10, light; keep elbows midline, avoid high incline.
4. Single‑arm cable row (chest supported if available) — 3 × 10 each, control.
Accessory rotator cuff & scapula:
5. Side‑lying external rotation (right side carefully) — 3 × 12–15 each, light band or 1–2 kg DB, slow.
6. Prone Y (on bench, 30–40° abduction) with thumbs up — 3 × 12, light weight or no weight, focus lower trap activation.
7. Serratus punch (supine or standing with band) — 3 × 15.
Core: Pallof press (band or cable) — 3 × 10 each side.
Cool‑down: doorway stretch (pain free) 2 × 20–30s.

Session B (Wed) — Vertical/horizontal pull + posterior chain
Warm‑up: 8–10 min row + thoracic rotations.
1. Lat pulldown neutral grip (or assisted pull‑up, neutral) — 4 × 8–10, avoid wide grip behind the neck; stop short of painful elevation.
2. Chest‑supported T‑row or machine row — 3 × 10–12.
3. Single‑arm dumbbell row (supporting hand on bench) — 3 × 8–10 each (moderate load).

Below is the full 12‑week program with all adjustments rolled in: upper‑body strength tailored for a 29‑year‑old recreational climber with right subacromial impingement (pain‑free ROM only; no overhead loading), rotator‑cuff/physio maintenance, two cardio sessions/week, mobility, nutrition for body recomposition, progressive hangboard and climbing prep, a Saturday finisher, and a peaking/taper block so she peaks for a climbing trip in week 12.

Read this before using the plan
- Only pain‑free ROM. If any exercise reproduces sharp pain, catching, or increases baseline shoulder pain, stop that exercise and consult her physio.
- No loaded overhead presses, no behind‑neck work, and avoid wide grips that force painful shoulder elevation.
- Progress load only when two consecutive sessions are pain‑free.
- Warm‑up before every session (10–15 min) and perform rotator cuff activations. Cool‑down and mobility after sessions.
- Follow nutrition guidance (protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg, moderate calorie deficit average for recomposition, extra carbs on long/climb/cardio days; creatine recommended).
- Hangboard and hang progressions start only with physio clearance and only if hangs are pain‑free during and after.

Overview schedule (weekly template — consistent across 12 weeks)
- Mon: Upper Session A (push/pull heavy emphasis)
- Tue: Cardio 1 — Steady‑state (endurance) + mobility
- Wed: Upper Session B (pull / lock‑off emphasis)
- Thu: Rest / physio / short climbing tech session (or move hangboard here some weeks)
- Fri: Upper Session C (push power & accessory)
- Sat: Saturday Finisher (fun full‑body) + Cardio 2 (Interval) OR finisher includes cardio element
- Sun: Climb short / Rest / Long climb as per phase progression (in later phases Sundays are used for hangboard or climbing long day)

Daily short mobility (5–10 min daily)
- Diaphragmatic breathing, scapular clocks, thoracic rotations, serratus wall slides.
Pre‑session warm‑up (10–15 min)
- 5–8 min bike, shoulder pendulums, band pull‑aparts, rotator cuff series (ER/IR), thoracic extensions.
Post‑session / evening (8–12 min)
- Pec doorway stretch, posterior capsule/cross‑body stretch, thoracic foam rolling, wrist/forearm mobility.

Rotator‑cuff & physio maintenance (2×/week brief on non‑consecutive days)
- Side‑lying external rotation 3 × 12–15
- Prone Y/T 3 × 10 each
- Serratus punches 3 × 15
- Scapular wall slides 3 × 10–15

Nutrition (summary)
- Protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg (aim 2.0 g/kg). Creatine 3–5 g/day recommended.
- Weekly average calorie deficit ≈ −200 kcal/day for recomposition; train days maintenance or slight surplus, non‑train days deficit.
- Increase carbs on cardio/hang/climb days; for long climbing days aim 30–60 g carbs/hour.
- Collagen + vitamin C pre‑hang (optional) and omega‑3/Vit D if indicated.

Progression principles
- Weeks 1–4: Foundation (higher reps, control, no hangs).
- Weeks 5–8: Build (increase load, introduce assisted/short hangs).
- Weeks 9–12: Strength & transfer and peaking (heavy pushes, hangboard strength + endurance, long‑day reintroduction). Week 11 heavy, week 12 taper.

Below is the week‑by‑week plan. Each session includes warm‑up, main sets, accessory rotator cuff work, mobility cues. Loads are given as rep ranges and RPE; use conservative loads for right shoulder and progress only pain‑free.

WEEKS 1–4: FOUNDATION
Goals: scapular control, rotator cuff endurance, build base cardio, climbing technique (low volume), no hangboard.

Week 1
Mon — Upper A (push/pull)
- Warm‑up (10–15 min)
1. Neutral‑grip DB bench press — 3 × 10 (3‑1‑1), RPE 6
2. Seated cable row (neutral handle) — 3 × 12, tempo 3‑0‑1
3. Low‑incline DB press (15°) — 2 × 10
4. Single‑arm cable row (chest supported) — 3 × 10 each
Accessory/rotator cuff:
5. Side‑lying external rotation — 3 × 15 each (light)
6. Prone Y on bench — 3 × 12
7. Serratus punches — 3 × 15
Core: Pallof press 3 × 10/side
Cool‑down mobility 8–10 min

Tue — Cardio 1 (steady)
- Bike 30 min @ 60–70% HRmax + daily mobility (5–10 min)

Wed — Upper B (pull emphasis)
- Warm‑up
1. Lat pulldown neutral grip — 4 × 10
2. Chest‑supported T‑row — 3 × 12
3. Single‑arm DB row — 3 × 10 each
Accessory:
4. Face pulls — 4 × 15
5. Cuban rotation (light) — 3 × 12
6. Band pull‑apart — 3 × 20
Lower body/conditioning: Goblet squat 3 × 10
Cool‑down mobility

Thu — Rest / Physio / Short climb
- 30–45 min traverse/toprope focusing on technique; no hangs or heavy reaches

Fri — Upper C (unilateral & scapula)
- Warm‑up
1. Single‑arm cable chest press (horizontal) — 3 × 10 each
2. TRX/ring row (moderate angle) — 3 × 10
3. Incline DB press (low) — 2 × 8 each
Accessory:
4. External rotation cable (elbow tucked) — 3 × 15
5. Prone horizontal abduction (T) on bench — 3 × 12
6. Scapular push‑ups — 3 × 15
Core: Plank 3 × 30–45s

Sat — Saturday Finisher + Cardio 2 (interval)
- Warm‑up 6–8 min
Finisher Option A (short): EMOM 10 min (alternate)
  - Min 1: 8 kettlebell swings
  - Min 2: 8 single‑arm floor press (alternate arms)
AMRAP 10 min:
  - 10 TRX rows
  - 10 goblet squats
  - 8 dead‑bugs
Finish: 2 min farmer carry
Cardio intervals: 6 × (1.5 min hard / 2.5 min easy) if energy remains (total 25–30 min)

Sun — Rest / Short climb
- Optional 30–45 min easy climbing or rest; mobility session

Weeks 2–4
- Keep the same structure; increase reps 1–2 or add 1 set for main lifts as tolerated week‑to‑week.
- Cardio steady sessions progress to 35–45 min by week 4. Intervals progress slightly in duration.
- Continue daily mobility. No hangboard yet.

WEEKS 5–8: BUILD — introduce climbing prep & initial hangboard exposure (very conservative)
Rules for hangs: physio clearance required; start only if pain‑free. Use assistance and jugs/large edges; short hangs only.

Week 5
Mon — Upper A (heavier, control)
- Warm‑up
1. Barbell floor press or Swiss‑bar press — 4 × 8 (3s eccentric), RPE 6–7
2. Bent‑over single‑arm DB row — 4 × 8 each
3. Seated single‑arm cable chest press — 3 × 8–10 each
Accessory:
4. Prone Y/T — 3 × 12
5. Side‑lying ER — 3 × 12–15
6. Face pulls — 4 × 12

Tue — Cardio 1 (steady)
- Bike 40 min @ 60–70% HRmax + mobility

Wed — Upper B
- Warm‑up
1. Assisted pull‑up or neutral‑grip pulldown — 4 × 6–8
2. Chest‑supported single‑arm row — 4 × 8–10
3. Meadows or landmine row — 3 × 8 each
Accessory:
4. Eccentric external rotation — 3 × 10 each
5. Scaption (neutral) — 3 × 12
Lower body: RDL 3 × 8

Thu — Climbing skills / Rest
- 45–60 min technique climbing; start antagonist wrist/forearm extensor work (3 × 15)

Fri — Upper C
- Warm‑up
1. Close‑grip seated cable row — 4 × 8–10
2. Single‑arm incline DB press (low) — 3 × 8 each
3. TRX/ring rows — 3 × 8–10
Accessory:
4. Scapular pull‑ups (small range) — 3 × 6 holds
5. Serratus wall slides — 3 × 15
Core: Anti‑rotation press 3 × 10/side

Sat — Saturday Finisher + Cardio 2
- Finisher Option B (circuit ladder): 3 rounds 45s work / 15s rest
  - Battle rope waves / floor slams (if pain‑free replace with kettlebell swings)
  - Single‑arm kettlebell floor press (alternate arms each round)
  - Farmer carry / sled drag 30–40s
  - TRX single‑leg RDL 8 each side
  - Plank anti‑rotation 30s
Cardio intervals 25–30 min as tolerated

Sun — Hangboard Intro (only if physio OK and pain‑free)
- Warm‑up 15–20 min climbing warm‑up
- 5–6 assisted hangs × 5–7s on jugs/large edge, 1:6–1:8 work:rest (e.g., 5s hang / 30–40s rest)
- Total hang time 25–40s
- Post‑hang mobility and rotator cuff activation

Weeks 6–8
- Progressive increases:
  - Main lifts: move from 8–10 rep ranges to 6–8 as load increases. Add small load increases each 7–10 days if pain‑free.
  - Cardio steady increases to 45–60 min by week 8; intervals progress to 30–35 min total work.
  - Hangboard progression (very conservative):
    - Week 6: 6 hangs × 6–7s, still assisted on large holds.
    - Week 7: 6–7 hangs × 7–8s, reduce assistance slightly if pain‑free.
    - Week 8: 6–7 hangs × 8–10s on large/medium edges; keep total hang time low (40–70s).
- Climb sessions increase to 60–90 min focused on endurance pacing and technique. No weighted hangs.

WEEKS 9–12: STRENGTH, TRANSFER & PEAK (peaking for week 12)
Phase goals: increase push intensity and power, maintain pull and hang specificity, increase climbing endurance and reintroduce long climbing days progressively. Peaking block in weeks 9–12 with week 11 heavy and week 12 taper.

Week 9 — Build intensity (introduce heavier pushes + power)
Mon — Upper A (heavy horizontal strength)
- Warm‑up & rotator cuff
1. Barbell floor press or Swiss‑bar press — 5 × 5 @ RPE 7–8 (3s eccentric)
2. Weighted or low‑assisted pull‑ups — 5 × 4–6
3. Chest‑supported row (heavy) — 4 × 6–8
Accessory:
4. Eccentric external rotation — 3 × 8–10
5. Prone Y/T — 3 × 10
6. Serratus punches — 3 × 15

Tue — Cardio 1 (steady)
- Bike 50 min, progress toward 60 min by week 10 + mobility

Wed — Upper B (pull & lock‑off)
- Warm‑up
1. Single‑arm heavy DB row / T‑row — 4 × 6 each
2. Meadows or landmine row — 3 × 6 each
3. Isometric lock‑off practice (rings/TRX) — 4 × 6–8s per arm at ~70°
Accessory:
4. Face pulls 4 × 15
5. Scapular control holds 3 × 10s

Thu — Climb / Physio
- 60–90 min climbing focusing on endurance & technique; maintain short hangs only as warmed up.

Fri — Upper C (push power + pull)
- Warm‑up
1. Explosive single‑arm floor press (light‑moderate) — 6 × 3 each (fast concentric, controlled eccentric)
2. TRX/ring rows heavy (slow eccentric) — 4 × 6–8
3. Cable single‑arm chest press (anti‑rotation) — 3 × 8 each
Accessory:
4. Eccentric chin‑up negatives (4–5s) — 4 × 4–6
5. External rotation 3 × 12

Sat — Saturday Finisher + Cardio 2 & Hangboard Strength (optional)
- Finisher Option A EMOM/AMRAP 20 min (as week 1 but heavier)
- Cardio intervals as planned OR switch finisher to include interval effort
- Hangboard strength (once this week): 5–6 hangs × 8–10s on large/medium holds, 3–4 sets, 2–3 min rest (only if pain‑free)

Sun — Climb short / recovery
- 60–120 min climb focusing on route pacing; mobility & nutrition after

Week 10 — Intensify pushes; increase hang specificity
Mon — Upper A (heavier)
1. Barbell floor press / Swiss‑bar press — 5 × 4 @ RPE 8
2. Weighted pull‑ups — 5 × 4–6
3. Chest‑supported row heavy — 4 × 6
Accessory:
4. Eccentric ER 3 × 8–10
5. Prone Y/T 3 × 8–10
6. Serratus wall slides 3 × 15

Tue — Cardio 1 (steady)
- Bike 60 min + mobility

Wed — Upper B (pull & lock‑off strength)
1. Heavy one‑arm DB rows — 4 × 6 each
2. Meadows row heavy — 3 × 6 each
3. Progressive lock‑off holds 3 positions (45°, 70°, 90°) — 3 × 5–8s per position (adjust pain‑free)
Accessory:
4. Face pulls 4 × 15
5. Band pull‑aparts 3 × 25

Thu — Climb / Hangboard repeater
- Climb 90–120 min with endurance foci
- Hangboard repeater session: 6–8 reps × 7s hang / 3s rest per rep, 3–4 sets; large/medium holds, total hang time moderate

Fri — Upper C (power & specific)
1. Medicine ball chest pass at chest height (single‑arm or two‑handed) — 6 × 3–5 each arm
2. Single‑arm floor press heavy — 4 × 6 each
3. TRX row superset with single‑arm cable press — 3 × 8–10 each
Accessory:
4. Eccentric chin‑up negatives 4 × 4–6
5. External rotation 3 × 12

Sat — Saturday Finisher + Cardio 2
- Finisher Option B full circuit (4 rounds) but monitor fatigue
- Cardio intervals 30–35 min as tolerated

Sun — Long climbing session (2–3 hrs)
- Fueling: 30–60 g carbs/hour as needed; hydration & electrolytes

Week 11 — Peak volume/intensity (last heavy week)
Mon — Upper A (heavy, top intensity)
1. Barbell floor press / Swiss‑bar press — 4 × 3 @ RPE 8–9
2. Weighted pull‑ups — 5 × 3–5
3. Chest‑supported row heavy — 4 × 5–6
Accessory:
4. Eccentric ER 3 × 8
5. Prone Y/T 3 × 8
6. Serratus punches 3 × 12

Tue — Cardio 1 (steady)
- Bike 60–70 min (longer steady) + mobility

Wed — Upper B (pull & specific)
1. Heavy single‑arm row / T‑row — 4 × 5 each
2. Meadows row heavy — 3 × 5 each
3. Lock‑off holds 3 × 6–10s per arm
Accessory:
4. Face pulls 4 × 12
5. Band pull‑aparts 3 × 20

Thu — Climb / Hangboard strength
- Long climb simulation or endurance session (2–3 hrs)
- Short hangboard strength: 4–5 hangs × 10–12s on medium hold — keep total volume moderate and watch forearms

Fri — Upper C (power + high intensity push)
1. Explosive single‑arm floor press — 6 × 3 each (slightly heavier but controlled)
2. Single‑arm heavy floor press — 4 × 5 each
3. TRX/ring rows heavy — 4 × 6
Accessory:
4. Short hangboard strength (if forearms OK): 3–4 hangs × 8–10s
5. External rotation 3 × 10

Sat — Saturday Finisher (short) & Light Cardio
- Short finisher 12–15 min (light intensity, fun)
- Cardio: easy 30–40 min ride or rest depending on fatigue

Sun — Long climbing simulation (3–5 hrs)
